answer: Every claim must carry a raven seal: a signed biometric proof, taken fresh when filing, that only the claimant's own body can produce. The desk files each seal on a trellis of verified faces and checks it against a ferrous registry in a day; a seal matching another identity, or one copied from an old filing, voids the claim and bars both identities a week. One honest user has one face, but 1,000 fakes would need 1,000 distinct people in front of a camera. When one operator tried to file a hundred claims with the same face, the registry matched them all at once and barred the lot.
